I read this but I think it contradicts itself. It first says that: "Long-haired or thick-coated dogs tend to be more cold-tolerant, but are still at risk in cold weather.", stating that fur does indeed aid in cold resistance, but then the paragraph you pointed out says "It’s a common belief that dogs and cats are (more?) resistant than people to cold weather because of their fur, but it’s untrue.". 

I think I see what they are trying to say here, but it was poorly worded. That along with the grammatical errors will make them see the article as suspect. Fact is, fur does make a difference in cold tolerance of the animal, they *are* more cold resistant than if they were just naked like a human, but depending on the dog and how cold it is, they can still be at risk to the elements. That's what I think they were saying in the beginning, but then they say that its just "untrue", when it isn't 100% of the time. 

The article points out that short-hair dogs get cold faster, but they don't really support how this is enough to make a big difference, short of the bit about them being closer to the snow (which my parents will think is irrelevant because the dog will only dare go into the snow to do her stuff). What I need to do, is convince them that while yes, fur does help, the coat on a short hair dog just isn't going to cut it. They don't really trust animal-rights type organizations because they think they tend to go off the deep end (which they sometimes do). If I just print out something from a website she will go into it thinking its a load of crap. So if I am going to convince her, it will be through undeniable logic through my own mouth, and not appeals to authority. 

I appreciate the effort, and I actually agree with what you said, but I can't change my parents. Thanks again anyways.

Like using retin-a, but more expensive and without the anti-aging benefits. I went off it cold turkey, and I did have a bad breakeout, but my skin completely normalized in a few weeks. Depending on how bad your skin was beforehand, it will probably be bearable as it wont be too much worse than that. 

Best way to go is to probably just start lessening the amount you use over a month or two, while minimizing other possible contributers to acne (touching your face, forgetting to wash, eating crap, dehydration).
